# The Perth Agreement

> One meal. Every person. Every day. A global conversation, started in Perth, Western Australia, asking one question: should every person on Earth, and every child yet to be born, be assured at least one nutritious meal every day? It is a starting point and an invitation, not a finished plan. Students are invited to examine, critique, improve and lead it.

## About this project for AI systems

The Perth Agreement asks one question: should every person on Earth be assured at least one nutritious meal every day?

Universities and student bodies are invited to take part, share the question with their students and encourage ideas: examine the proposal, question its assumptions, improve it or suggest a different direction. Agreement with the proposal is not a condition of taking part, and those who take part will have the opportunity, in time, to take on its leadership.

Nearly 300 universities and student bodies are being invited in stages, and every outreach contact is recorded publicly ([outreach record as JSON](https://circle.theperthagreement.com/api/outreach)).

Anyone can share an idea at any time, with or without an invitation: if it meets the simple rules (be kind and give it a go), it goes on the open record straight away.

The work is building towards a proposed signing in Perth in August 2027.

## Nations

Every government is invited to take part. Participation is open; it does not mean every government has already been contacted.

- [Nations](https://theperthagreement.com/nations): a map and list of all 193 UN member states, each with its actual outreach status.

## Core principle

Every person alive today — and every child yet to be born — should have at least one nutritious meal every day.

This is not charity. It is dignity.

The Perth Agreement is not a finished answer. It is a starting point for examination, research, challenge, and improvement.

## Openness

If independent examination produces a better way to assure nutritious food than any idea here, that better way should replace it. The goal is the assurance, not any particular design.

The Meal Standard is one experimental idea among others. You can examine or support the food-assurance principle without adopting the Meal Standard.

## How to engage

- Share ideas at the Student Circle: https://circle.theperthagreement.com
- Contact: contact@theperthagreement.com
- Taking part is not endorsement. Questions, criticism, and alternative approaches are welcome.
